title: Async deadlocks and livelock
summary: SemaphoreSlim is not reentrant, async deadlocks hold no thread, and livelock looks busy while doing nothing.

steps.title: The deadlock that holds no thread
body: `lock` cannot contain `await`, so async code protects state with `SemaphoreSlim(1, 1)`:
```csharp fragment
public async Task AddManyAsync(IEnumerable<string> items)
await _gate.WaitAsync();
try { foreach (var i in items) await AddAsync(i); }   // AddAsync also does: await _gate.WaitAsync()
finally { _gate.Release(); }
Unlike `Monitor`, a semaphore is **not reentrant** and has no owner: `AddAsync` waits for the slot that `AddManyAsync` holds, and
`AddManyAsync` waits for `AddAsync`. Forever.
In a dump this looks like *nothing*: no thread is blocked, `syncblk` is empty, the pool threads are idle. The request's state
machines sit on the heap, each awaiting the next. `dumpasync` (or Visual Studio's Parallel Stacks in **Tasks** view) shows the chain:
`AddManyAsync` awaiting `AddAsync` awaiting `SemaphoreSlim.WaitAsync`.
Fix: take the semaphore only at the **public entry points**, and have them call private `...Core` methods that assume it is held.

steps.prompt: Requests to `/cart/bulk` never finish. CPU is idle, `dotnet-counters` shows a normal thread count and an empty queue, and `syncblk` lists nothing. Where do you look next?
options: `dumpasync` in the dump, to see which async methods are stuck awaiting what
steps.explain: Nothing is blocked and the pool is healthy, so this is not starvation or a Monitor deadlock. Code that awaits forever holds no thread; only the async view shows it.

items: A method holding `SemaphoreSlim(1,1)` calls another public method that waits on the same semaphore
A method holding a `lock` calls another method that locks the same object
`await _gate.WaitAsync();` with `Release()` only on the success path
Public methods take the semaphore and call private `Core` methods that do not
Two async methods take two semaphores in opposite orders
steps.explain: Monitor (`lock`) is reentrant for the owning thread; SemaphoreSlim is not reentrant at all. Lock ordering applies to semaphores exactly as to locks.

steps.title: Livelock: busy, polite and stuck
body: In a **livelock** threads are not blocked; they keep reacting to each other and never make progress. Two threads that each take one
lock, try the other with `Monitor.TryEnter`, fail, release and retry *at the same moment* can repeat that forever. CPU is high,
nothing completes.
The same thing happens between services: two clients retrying a conflict immediately (optimistic concurrency, a lease) keep
colliding. The cure is the same: **randomised backoff** (jitter) so that the retries drift apart, or a fixed order so there is no
conflict to retry.
| | Deadlock | Livelock | Starvation |
| CPU | idle | busy | low (pool) or one thread never scheduled |
| Threads | blocked | running | blocked or waiting for a turn |
| Evidence | `syncblk`, `clrstack` | same stacks in every sample, rising retry counters | `dotnet-counters`, thread count climbing |

steps.prompt: Match the symptom to the problem.
pairs: CPU at 100%, the same retry log line thousands of times, nothing completes
CPU idle, two threads each holding a lock the other wants
CPU low, thread count rising 1-2 per second, queue growing
No thread blocked, async requests never complete

steps.title: A cart that does not wait for itself
prompt: `Cart.AddManyAsync` hangs forever: it holds the semaphore and calls `AddAsync`, which waits for the same semaphore.
Fix **`Cart`** so that every public method (`AddAsync`, `AddManyAsync`, `CountAsync`) is still safe to call concurrently and none
of them can wait for itself. Keep the names and signatures.
starter: try { foreach (var item in items) await AddAsync(item); }
solution: try { foreach (var item in items) await AddCoreAsync(item); }
template: var dojoFinished = await Task.WhenAny(dojoMany, Task.Delay(2000)) == dojoMany;
Dojo.Check("AddManyAsync finishes", dojoFinished, "It was still waiting after 2 seconds: it waits for a semaphore it already holds.");
Dojo.Eq("Three items were added", 3, await dojoCart.CountAsync());
var dojoAll = Task.WhenAll(Enumerable.Range(0, 20).Select(i => i % 2 == 0 ? dojoCart.AddAsync($"x{i}") : dojoCart.AddManyAsync(new[] { $"y{i}", $"z{i}" })));
var dojoAllDone = await Task.WhenAny(dojoAll, Task.Delay(3000)) == dojoAll;
Dojo.Check("Concurrent adds all finish", dojoAllDone, "Some calls never finished.");
Dojo.Eq("No item is lost under concurrent calls", 3 + 10 + 20, await dojoCart.CountAsync());
hints: Move the actual add into a private method that does **not** touch the semaphore, and call it from both public methods.
`private async Task AddCoreAsync(string item) { await Task.Yield(); _items.Add(item); }`; `AddManyAsync` loops over `AddCoreAsync`.
